findings.asked: A multi-step trigonometry problem in non-right-angled triangles.
findings.wentWrong: Nearly 40% solved it; over 40% could not find a first step; the rest used some trigonometry sensibly but did not see how to finish.
findings.rule: Decide which triangle has enough information to start, and say why.

findings.asked: Closing question needing the cosine rule, sine rule and the area formula after adding one line to the diagram.
findings.wentWrong: About a sixth got full marks; many attempted it. The unlock was drawing one extra line.
findings.fullMarkAnswersDid: Added the line that created a triangle with three known pieces, then moved through cosine rule, sine rule and half ab sin C in order.
findings.rule: If no triangle is solvable, draw a line that makes one.

findings.asked: A testing trigonometry question with a specific correct starting point.
findings.wentWrong: Weaker candidates did not see that the cosine rule had to come first.
findings.rule: Three sides, or two sides and the included angle: cosine rule first.

findings.asked: Equal areas to find a side, then the cosine rule.
findings.wentWrong: Nearly a third finished; weaker candidates could not find a logical start; many wrote the equal-area equation and stopped.
findings.rule: Area = half ab sin C can be solved for a side, then feed it into the cosine rule.

findings.asked: Bearings combined with the sine rule.
findings.wentWrong: About a quarter got full marks; converting bearings into the triangle's angles was the hurdle.
findings.rule: Mark every angle from the bearings on the diagram before choosing a rule.

findings.asked: Areas and the cosine rule in an eight-mark final problem.
findings.wentWrong: Most scored some marks; about a quarter got all eight.
findings.rule: Plan the chain: which rule gives which unknown, in what order.

ruleToRemember: Two sides and the included angle, or three sides: cosine rule. A side-angle pair: sine rule. Area = half ab sin C. If nothing is solvable, add one line; carry full accuracy between stages.
aStarSignal: Seeing the auxiliary line and planning a three-rule chain (cosine, sine, area) before writing anything.
